text:
Maya (growth): Morning — proposing a compact welcome sequence we’re calling 'Morning Glide'. Short cadence, timezone-aware, invites to a quick benchmarks webinar in email 3.
Jon (marketing): Love the name. Goal is trial activation within 7 days, right? :rocket:
Maya (growth): Yep. Primary metric: trial->first-inference call within 7 days. Secondary: webinar RSVPs from high-intent segments.
Lia (design): For subject lines I can mock a few—keeping it clean for mobile: 'Quick start with Redwood: 5 mins', 'Your first inference in minutes'. Want 3 variants for A/B.
Sam (content): Draft copy for email 1 (welcome):
```
Hey {{first_name}},
Welcome to Redwood — quick tips to get your first inference running.
1) Try the hosted API with our one-click sample.
2) See cost/latency tips for dev builds.
3) Join a short webinar if you want an intro walkthrough.
See you in the dashboard — Sam
```
Will iterate tone to be more product-focused for platform teams.
Oliver (ops): Send windows? We should honor local mornings (08:00-10:30 local). Can we bucket by tz and company size?
Maya (growth): Yes — three buckets: local morning, local afternoon, and global-night (for APAC). Priority for morning sends is higher for engagement.
Jon (marketing): Segmentation rules idea:
- Segment A: trial started in last 48h + api_key created -> early-activation flow (email 1 + in-email quickstart)
- Segment B: signed up but no API key -> nurture + checklist
- Segment C: enterprise / SSO flagged -> route to dedicated rep + invite to executive webinar
Lia (design): I'll prepare mobile-first templates + a compact CTA block for the quickstart snippet.
Sam (content): Email 3 includes webinar invite + benchmark narrative one-pager link. Draft subject variants: 'See Redwood vs. open alternatives (latency & cost)', 'Join a 20-min demo + benchmarks'.
Maya (growth): A/B plan: Subject A = product benefit, Subject B = benchmark curiosity. Send A/B to 20/20/60 split across Segment A and B.
Oliver (ops): send-bot -> can we schedule time-windowed sends and stagger 10m between large cohorts to avoid rate spikes?
send-bot: Campaign 'morning-glide-2123456789' scheduled. Windows: tz-aware 08:00-10:30, 10m staging between cohort bursts.
Jon (marketing): Tracking: UTM tags for each subject variant and segment, separate event for 'clicked quickstart' and 'webinar-rsvp'. Sam will add short survey link in email 4 for quality feedback.
Sam (content): Quick copy test for email 2 (no technical call): 'Three ways teams cut inference cost by 30% — tips + config snippets.' Includes 2 inline code examples for batching config.
Lia (design): I'll also make a 1-image highlight for the benchmark PDF preview — keep under 100kb for inbox speed.
Maya (growth): Risk check: If someone RSVPs to webinar, block them from email 4 (repeat invites). If they convert (first inference), mark them out of drip.
Jon (marketing): Canary send plan: 200 recipients internal + partners at 09:00 tomorrow, then scale after 4h review.
Oliver (ops): Noted. I'll monitor rate and error traces that morning; set an alert if bounce rate > 3% or API errors spike.
Maya (growth): Can we add a soft personalization: if product_interest tag == 'dedicated' show one sentence about Dedicated pools? Otherwise default hosted copy.
Sam (content): Yep. Small blocks per interest tag. Also add 'privacy & security' blurb for private deployment prospects.
Lia (design): Final assets ready by EOD today, I'll drop in the campaign folder.
Jon (marketing): I'll schedule the canary and the A/B with send-bot, link the KPI dashboard.
Maya (growth): Great. Action items: Sam copy refine by 3pm, Lia templates by EOD, Oliver to confirm staging windows, Jon to set canary. Check back here with send confirmation. :thumbsup:
